title: Scheduling Worksheet: Ship Date Set When a Hold Is Released (Factory Production Orders)
content:
For Factory Production Orders, the ship date set at the release of a customer hold is fixed as follows.

**Requoted ship date.** The requoted ship date is the release date plus the class standard lead time in business days, counted starting the day after the release date, Monday through Friday excluding U.S. federal holidays.

**Release date.** The release date is the handling date on which the hold is released.

**Figure recorded.** The figure recorded at release is the requoted ship date written as the number of calendar days from the release date to that date.

## Inputs

| Input | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| release date | the handling date of the release |
| class standard lead time | the build class of the order (business days) |

## Worked example (hypothetical, no federal holiday in the period)

A Custom Color Build order, whose class standard lead time is 30 business days, is released from hold on a Monday. Counting starts on the Tuesday: 4 business days in the release week and 5 in each following week reach the 29th business day on the Friday five weeks later and the 30th on the Monday six weeks after the release. From the release Monday to that Monday is 42 calendar days, so the figure recorded at release is 42.

Equivalent statement: the requoted ship date is the 30th business day after the release date; written for the record, it is 42 calendar days out.

## Points of reading

- Saturdays, Sundays and U.S. federal holidays are skipped in the business-day count.
- The figure recorded is a calendar-day count from the release date, so a release on a Friday and one on the following Monday with the same business-day lead record different figures.
